in.why: Say a before a job word.

native.hook: 「I am student」で止まってない？
native.tip: 職業の前には a が必要。日本語にない「a」を忘れずに！
native.caption: “I am student.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語には冠詞がないので、つい抜けがち。職業の前には a をつけます。 “I am a student.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“a”。a を入れて自然な英語に。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you stop at “I am student”?
en.tip: Put a before a job word. Japanese has no a, so it is easy to forget!
en.caption: Do you say “I am student.”? 😅 Japanese has no articles, so a often goes missing. Put a before a job. The natural way is “I am a student.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Child has a special plural: children.

native.hook: two child、複数形が抜けてない？
native.tip: 2つ以上なら複数形。child の複数形は children（childs ではない）。
native.caption: “I have two child.”と言っていませんか？😅 数が2以上のときは名詞を複数形にします。child は特別で children になります。 “I have two children.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“books”。数が2以上なら名詞は複数形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Is your plural missing in “two child”?
en.tip: With two or more, use the plural. Child becomes children.
en.caption: Do you say “I have two child.”? 😅 With two or more, the noun must be plural. Child is special: children. The natural way is “I have two children.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: With yesterday, use the simple past.

native.hook: yesterday と have seen？注意！
native.tip: 「昨日」など過去の時を言うなら、過去形 saw を使います。
native.caption: “I have seen him yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 yesterday のように過去の時がはっきりしているときは、現在完了ではなく過去形を使います。 “I saw him yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“saw”。yesterday には過去形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: With a clear past time like yesterday, use the simple past.
en.caption: Do you say “I have seen him yesterday.”? 😅 With a clear past time such as yesterday, use the simple past, not the present perfect. The natural way is “I saw him yesterday.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Arrive goes with at, not to.
in.answer_say: At! I arrived at the station.

native.hook: 「到着する」に to を使ってない？
native.tip: arrive の後は場所なら at、都市なら in を使います。to は使いません。
native.caption: “I arrived to the station.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「に」につられて to を使いがち。arrive の後は at を使います。 “I arrived at the station.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“at”。arrive のあとは at か in。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After arrive, use at for places or in for cities. Not to.
en.caption: Do you say “I arrived to the station.”? 😅 The Japanese “ni” pulls you to use to, but after arrive you say at. The natural way is “I arrived at the station.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: A mansion is a very big house.

quiz.stem: I rent a small ___ near the station.

in.answer_say: Apartment! I rent a small apartment.

native.hook: 「マンション」は英語で通じない
native.tip: 英語の mansion は大豪邸。日本のマンションは apartment と言います。
native.caption: “My mansion is small.”と言っていませんか？😅 英語の mansion は「大豪邸」のこと。日本でいうマンションは apartment（または condo）です。 “My apartment is small.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“apartment”。mansion は大豪邸のこと。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: A mansion is a huge house. Use apartment for a Japanese manshon.
en.caption: Do you say “My mansion is small.”? 😅 In English a mansion is a huge house. A Japanese manshon is an apartment. The natural way is “My apartment is small.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say excited, not high tension.
in.answer_say: Excited! I am excited about the trip.

native.hook: 「ハイテンション」は和製英語
native.tip: tension は「緊張」の意味。盛り上がっているなら excited を使おう。
native.caption: “I am high tension today.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「ハイテンション」は和製英語です。英語の tension は緊張や不安のこと。元気なら excited と言います。 “I am so excited today.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“excited”。ハイテンションは和製英語。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Tension means stress. When you feel full of energy, say excited.
en.caption: Do you say “I am high tension today.”? 😅 High tension is Japanese-made English. Tension means stress. Say excited instead. The natural way is “I am so excited today.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: We make a mistake, not do.

native.hook: mistake は do じゃなくて make
native.tip: 「間違える」は make a mistake。do は使いません。セットで覚えよう。
native.caption: “I did a mistake.”と言っていませんか？😅 「間違いをする」を do で訳したくなりますが、英語では make a mistake がセットの言い方です。 “I made a mistake.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“made”。make a mistake で一つの表現。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Is it “do” a mistake? Not really!
en.tip: Say make a mistake. Learn the two words together.
en.caption: Do you say “I did a mistake.”? 😅 You might translate suru as do, but English says make a mistake as a set phrase. The natural way is “I made a mistake.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say on foot for walking.
in.answer_say: On! I go to school on foot.

native.hook: 「歩いて」は by walk じゃない
native.tip: 乗り物は by、歩きは on foot。決まったセットで言います。
native.caption: “I go there by walk.”と言っていませんか？😅 電車は by train なので、歩きも by walk と言いたくなります。でも歩きは on foot が決まり文句です。 “I go there on foot.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“on”。歩きは on foot。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: For vehicles use by. For walking, say on foot.
en.caption: Do you say “I go there by walk.”? 😅 By train works, so by walk feels logical. But for walking the set phrase is on foot. The natural way is “I go there on foot.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Agree is a verb. No am.

native.hook: 「I am agree」になってない？
native.tip: agree は動詞なので be 動詞はいりません。I agree でOK！
native.caption: “I am agree.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「賛成だ」につられて am を入れがち。agree はそれだけで動詞なので、I agree と言います。 “I agree.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“agree”。be 動詞は不要です。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Agree is already a verb, so no am is needed. Just say I agree.
en.caption: Do you say “I am agree.”? 😅 Japanese sansei da makes you add am. But agree is a verb by itself: I agree. The natural way is “I agree.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: We take medicine, we do not eat it.
in.answer_say: Take! I take medicine every day.

native.hook: 薬を「食べる」は英語で言わない
native.tip: 薬は「飲む」でも take を使います。drink や eat は使いません。
native.caption: “I ate medicine.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「薬を飲む」を drink と訳しがちですが、英語では take medicine と言います。 “I took medicine.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“take”。薬は take。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Use take for medicine. Not eat or drink.
en.caption: Do you say “I ate medicine.”? 😅 You may translate kusuri wo nomu as drink, but English says take medicine. The natural way is “I took medicine.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am difficult to get up early.
in.right: It is hard for me to get up early.
in.why: Difficult is for things, not for people.
in.memory: It is hard for me to get up early.

quiz.stem: ___ is hard for me to wake up.

in.answer_say: It! It is hard for me to wake up.

native.hook: 「私は難しい」になってない？
native.tip: difficult や hard の主語は人ではなく It。It is hard for me to ~ の形で。
native.caption: “I am difficult to get up early.”と言っていませんか？😅 「私は早起きが難しい」と主語を I にすると不自然に。difficult は物事に使うので、It を主語にします。 “It is hard for me to get up early.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“It”。It is hard for me to ～ の形を使おう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Hard and difficult describe things. Start with It is hard for me to...
en.caption: Do you say “I am difficult to get up early.”? 😅 Making I the subject sounds odd. Difficult describes things, so start with It. The natural way is “It is hard for me to get up early.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Many people is in the park.
in.right: Many people are in the park.
in.why: People is plural. Use are.
in.memory: Many people are in the park.

native.hook: people は単数？複数？
native.tip: people は複数扱い。is ではなく are を使います。
native.caption: “Many people is in the park.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語では人数に関係なく同じ形ですが、英語の people は複数扱い。動詞は are になります。 “Many people are in the park.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“are”。people は複数扱い。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: People is plural. Use are, not is.
en.caption: Do you say “Many people is in the park.”? 😅 Japanese does not change form, but English people is plural, so the verb is are. The natural way is “Many people are in the park.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I have a lot of homework.
in.why: Homework has no plural.
in.memory: I have a lot of homework.
in.answer_say: Homework! I have too much homework.

native.hook: homeworks に s をつけてない？
native.tip: homework は数えられない名詞。s は付けず、a lot of で量を表します。
native.caption: “I have many homeworks.”と言っていませんか？😅 homework は数えられない名詞なので、s は付けません。たくさんは many ではなく a lot of を使います。 “I have a lot of homework.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“homework”。数えられない名詞に s は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you add s to homework?
en.tip: Homework cannot be counted. No s. Say a lot of homework.
en.caption: Do you say “I have many homeworks.”? 😅 Homework is uncountable, so no s. For a large amount, use a lot of. The natural way is “I have a lot of homework.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Past time needs a past verb.

native.hook: 過去の話なのに eat のまま？
native.tip: 日本語は動詞が変わらないことも。英語は過去の話なら ate のように変えます。
native.caption: “I eat natto yesterday.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語では「昨日」があれば動詞はそのままでも通じます。でも英語では動詞そのものを過去形に変えます。 “I ate natto yesterday.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“ate”。昨日の話は過去形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: English changes the verb for the past: eat becomes ate.
en.caption: Do you say “I eat natto yesterday.”? 😅 In Japanese, yesterday is enough. In English the verb itself must change. The natural way is “I ate natto yesterday.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Time here has no a.
in.answer_say: Any! I don't have any time.

native.hook: 「時間がない」に a は不要
native.tip: 「時間」の意味の time は数えられない名詞。a は付けません。
native.caption: “I don't have a time.”と言っていませんか？😅 「時間」という意味の time は数えられない名詞です。a は付けず、I don't have time と言います。 “I don't have time.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“any”。時間の time に a は不要。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you say “I don't have a time”?
en.tip: Time meaning free time has no a. Say I don't have time.
en.caption: Do you say “I don't have a time.”? 😅 Time as free time is uncountable, so no a. Say I don't have time. The natural way is “I don't have time.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: In a taxi, on a train!
in.why: Small cars use in. Big ones use on.
in.answer_say: In! I got in the taxi.

native.hook: タクシーに「on」で乗ってない？
native.tip: 車・タクシーは in、電車・バスは on。乗り物の大きさで使い分けます。
native.caption: “I got on the taxi.”と言っていませんか？😅 車やタクシーのような小さい乗り物は in、電車やバスのような大きい乗り物は on を使います。 “I got in the taxi.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“in”。車は in、電車は on。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Use in for cars and taxis. Use on for trains and buses.
en.caption: Do you say “I got on the taxi.”? 😅 Small vehicles like cars and taxis use in. Big ones like trains and buses use on. The natural way is “I got in the taxi.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Put very much after the thing.
in.answer_say: Much! I like cats very much.

native.hook: 「とても好き」は very like？
native.tip: very は動詞の前に置けません。like ～ very much の順にします。
native.caption: “I very like pizza.”と言っていませんか？😅 「とても好き」を I very like と言いたくなりますが、英語では very much を文の後ろに置きます。 “I like pizza very much.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“much”。very much は後ろに置きます。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Very cannot go before a verb. Say like it very much.
en.caption: Do you say “I very like pizza.”? 😅 I very like is tempting, but English puts very much after the object. The natural way is “I like pizza very much.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I listen to music every day.
in.why: Listen needs to before the thing.
in.memory: I listen to music every day.

native.hook: 「音楽を聞く」で to が消えてる
native.tip: listen は「listen to ～」の形。to を忘れずに！
native.caption: “I listen music every day.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「音楽を聞く」には「を」しかないので、to が抜けがち。listen のあとは to が必要です。 “I listen to music every day.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“to”。listen のあとは to。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Listen always needs to before the thing you hear.
en.caption: Do you say “I listen music every day.”? 😅 Japanese uses wo only, so to gets lost. English needs listen to. The natural way is “I listen to music every day.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: After can, use the plain verb.

native.hook: can のあとに to を入れてない？
native.tip: can のあとは動詞の原形だけ。to はいりません。
native.caption: “She can to speak English.”と言っていませんか？😅 can のような助動詞のあとには、to なしの動詞の原形が続きます。be able to と混ざらないように。 “She can speak English.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“speak”。can のあとは原形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After can, use the plain verb. No to.
en.caption: Do you say “She can to speak English.”? 😅 After a modal like can, the base verb follows without to. Do not mix it with be able to. The natural way is “She can speak English.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: After doesn't, the verb has no s.

native.hook: doesn't のあとに s をつけてない？
native.tip: doesn't がすでに三単現の s を持っているので、動詞は原形に。
native.caption: “He doesn't likes it.”と言っていませんか？😅 否定文では doesn't が三人称単数を担当します。そのため like は s のない原形になります。 “He doesn't like it.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“like”。doesn't のあとは原形。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Do you add s after doesn't?
en.tip: Doesn't already carries the s. Use the plain verb: like.
en.caption: Do you say “He doesn't likes it.”? 😅 In negatives, doesn't handles the third person, so the verb stays plain. The natural way is “He doesn't like it.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: If you don't, say no.

quiz.stem: You don't like fish? ___, I don't.

native.hook: Yes か No か？日本人の癖の罠！
native.tip: 英語では事実で答えます。否定なら No と言います。
native.caption: “Yes, I don't like fish.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語は相手の言葉に同意するかで「はい」と答えますが、英語は答えの内容が否定なら No です。 “No, I don't like fish.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“No”。否定の答えは No。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.hook: Yes or No? Japanese habit trap!
en.tip: In English, answer by the fact. If it is negative, say No.
en.caption: Do you say “Yes, I don't like fish.”? 😅 Japanese says hai to agree with the question. English says No if your answer is negative. The natural way is “No, I don't like fish.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Use a full phrase: I'm late.

native.hook: 「遅れてごめん」の言い方は？
native.tip: Sorry for late は不自然。Sorry I'm late. と主語と動詞を入れます。
native.caption: “Sorry for late.”と言っていませんか？😅 日本語の「遅れてごめん」をそのまま訳すと不自然に。Sorry のあとは I'm late と文の形にします。 “Sorry I'm late.” が自然な言い方です。Amaの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“late”。I'm late と文で言おう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: Say Sorry I'm late. Use a full sentence after sorry.
en.caption: Do you say “Sorry for late.”? 😅 A word-for-word translation sounds odd. After sorry, say a full phrase: I'm late. The natural way is “Sorry I'm late.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I went there by the plane.
in.why: With by, do not add the.

native.hook: by the plane？ the はいらない
native.tip: 乗り物の手段を言う by のあとには the も a も付けません。
native.caption: “I went there by the plane.”と言っていませんか？😅 「〜で行く」と手段を言うときは by plane、by train のように冠詞なしで言います。 “I went there by plane.” が自然な言い方です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“plane”。by のあとは冠詞なし。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: After by, name the vehicle with no a or the.
en.caption: Do you say “I went there by the plane.”? 😅 To say how you travel, use by plane or by train with no article. The natural way is “I went there by plane.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
